title: cli breaks on certain prompts which contain code logs

triage_metadata.reasoning: No source files were pruned; all PR modifications directly address the reported issue.

summary.problem: The CLI crashes with filesystem errors (such as ENAMETOOLONG) when user prompts contain test logs or stack traces.
summary.root_cause: The CLI misinterprets large text blocks and log fragments (containing markers like `AssertionError:`, `FAIL `, or `TestingLibraryElementError:`) as file paths and attempts to resolve them via system filesystem APIs without validating path length or structure.
summary.context: Pasting terminal output or test failure logs into the CLI causes @-command path resolution and Config.validatePathAccess to execute filesystem operations on malformed strings.

steps: Create `validatePath` in `packages/core/src/utils/path-validator.ts` to check input paths against control/newline characters (`/[\n\r\0\t]/`), log markers (`/(^|[/\\])(AssertionError:|FAIL |✓ |× |TestingLibraryElementError:)/`), suspicious quotes/ellipses, and length limits (`MAX_PATH_LENGTH = 4096`, `MAX_COMPONENT_LENGTH = 255`).
Implement `resolveAtCommandPath` and `tryExtractPath` in `packages/core/src/utils/atCommandUtils.ts` to validate @-command paths and extract valid embedded file paths from log fragments.
Update `Config.validatePathAccess` in `packages/core/src/config/config.ts` to call `validatePath` before performing permission checks.
Refactor `resolveFilePaths` in `packages/cli/src/ui/hooks/atCommandProcessor.ts` to use `resolveAtCommandPath` instead of directly calling `fs.stat` on raw path strings.
Refactor path resolution in `packages/cli/src/acp/acpSession.ts` to use `resolveAtCommandPath` for safe path lookup and permission dialog prompts.

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: Malformed paths and log snippets are recognized as invalid or best-effort recovered without triggering filesystem crashes.
verification_steps: Run unit tests for path validation: `npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/utils/path-validator.test.ts`.
Verify `validatePath` rejects paths with newlines, control characters, log markers (`AssertionError:`, `FAIL`), and path lengths exceeding 4096 characters.
Verify that valid paths with apostrophes, spaces, or brackets remain valid.
